data.title: Microbiota-associated kynurenic acid drives PD-1 blockade resistance through an ITGA2-mTOR-CTSV axis in gastric cancer.
data.authors: Ren Y; Yu X; Jiang J; Luo J; Zhao C; et al.

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Tumor microbiota-derived kynurenic acid drives resistance to PD-1 blockade in gastric cancer through the ITGA2-mTOR-CTSV axis: kynurenic acid induces ITGA2 and inhibits an mTOR-dependent cascade, which sustains cathepsin V expression and suppresses CD8+ T cell cytotoxic function.
data.abstract_excerpt: The tumor microbiota critically shapes responses to immunotherapy; however, the mechanisms by which specific microbial species drive immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) resistance in gastric cancer (GC) remain poorly defined. Bacterial enrichment was assessed in ICB-unresponsive GC tissues from patients and multiple preclinical models. Orthotopic, subcutaneous, and germ-free mono-colonized mouse models were employed to evaluate the impact on antitumor immunity and PD-1 blockade efficacy.

extracted_findings.effect: Kynurenic acid induces ITGA2 and inhibits an mTOR-dependent cascade, sustaining cathepsin V and suppressing CD8+ T cells, driving immunotherapy resistance
